title: IMDO OSINT — October 13, 2026 — 11:23 PM New York

sections.title: Wars and Armed Conflicts
sections.shortfall: Three distinct developments met the late-edition threshold; two slots remain open.

entries.title: Iran shifts tactics as attacks on Hormuz shipping accelerate
entries.development: Two senior Iranian officials told Reuters that Iran is changing the type and pace of attacks on Strait of Hormuz shipping to keep oil prices high before the U.S. midterms; independent incident data recorded at least five events in 48 hours.
entries.significance: The reported strategy turns commercial shipping into an instrument of electoral and economic coercion, raising risks for crews, insurance and energy flows.
entries.uncertainty: Strategic intent is attributed to officials; individual incident attribution remains case-specific.

entries.title: Kyiv missile strike death toll rises to two, with 21 injured
entries.development: Material update: officials said five ballistic missiles hit Kyiv, killing two and injuring 21; a residential tower and thermal power plant were struck in the second attack within 24 hours.
entries.significance: The casualty and target confirmation sharpens the evidence that the announced energy truce lacks effective implementation and early-warning continuity.
entries.uncertainty: Russia’s target rationale and the cause of the warning failure were not independently established.

entries.title: Oil prices rise as markets price Saudi and Hormuz risks
entries.development: Oil prices rose as traders assessed Houthi threats to Saudi supply, accelerated Hormuz attacks and possible Russian diesel flows.
entries.significance: Price movement is an imperfect but immediate measure of whether announced diplomatic and supply measures offset physical shipping danger.
entries.uncertainty: This is market response, not proof of future supply loss or a price forecast.

sections.title: Sociopolitical Shifts
sections.shortfall: Three distinct developments met the threshold; two slots remain open.

entries.title: French student protest turnout declines but remains nationwide
entries.development: Reuters counted more than 161,000 demonstrators and 214 closed schools, down from 266,000 participants and 800 closures the prior week, while clashes continued in several cities.
entries.significance: The movement is contracting from its peak without disappearing, giving a clearer measure of durability than isolated crowd images.
entries.uncertainty: Police, union and organizer estimates may differ.

entries.title: NYC business influence becomes an explicit gubernatorial campaign issue
entries.development: James Dolan publicly pressed the Partnership for New York City to support Republican Bruce Blakeman against Governor Kathy Hochul; the Partnership said it does not endorse candidates.
entries.significance: The dispute exposes pressure on formally nonpartisan business institutions to convert policy advocacy into direct electoral intervention.
entries.uncertainty: The report describes advocacy and campaign spending, not evidence that the Partnership changed policy.

entries.title: Bank of America receives $1.2 billion sanctions penalty
entries.development: AP’s late political briefing reports a $1.2 billion penalty against Bank of America for sanctions violations.
entries.significance: A penalty of this scale may influence compliance spending and how banks police politically exposed or restricted transactions.
entries.uncertainty: The accessed briefing did not provide the underlying order, covered transactions or admission language.

sections.title: NYC Affairs
sections.shortfall: Three new public-record developments were identified; two slots remain open.

entries.title: Council hearing examines voucher homeownership participation
entries.development: The Public Housing Committee calendar lists Intro 1082-2026, requiring annual reporting on city-household participation in the Housing Choice Voucher homeownership program, at 250 Broadway.
entries.significance: Regular reporting could reveal whether a rarely used federal pathway is reaching voucher households and where counseling, lender or supply barriers occur.
entries.uncertainty: The listing confirms the hearing item, not passage or implementation.

entries.title: Council schedules oversight of block-by-block housing planning
entries.development: The Land Use Committee scheduled an October 21 oversight hearing on planning and development under the mayor’s block-by-block housing plan; written testimony is accepted for 72 hours afterward.
entries.significance: The hearing creates a concrete venue to press for project maps, affordability levels, displacement safeguards and delivery milestones.
entries.implications: Testimony may be sent to landusetestimony@council.nyc.gov.

entries.title: HPD hearing will revisit terms of a Harlem land disposition
entries.development: Newly discovered older notice: HPD will hear proposed amendments to a deed and land-disposition agreement at the 224 West 124th Street Library.
entries.significance: Changes to disposition terms can alter affordability, development deadlines or enforcement obligations long after public land is conveyed.
entries.uncertainty: The accessible excerpt did not expose the parcels or exact amendments; those documents should be reviewed before testimony.

sections.title: The State of Downtown
sections.shortfall: Three public organizer listings met the standard. Signed-in Instagram was unavailable; two slots remain open.

entries.title: Sonic Spectrum gathers Harlem artists around music
entries.development: The Children’s Art Carnival will open Sonic Spectrum, a group exhibition of Harlem artists responding to music; regular gallery hours are Saturday and Sunday, noon–6 PM.
entries.significance: The exhibition connects neighborhood visual practice with musical culture through a community-rooted institution.
entries.uncertainty: Opening time and admission price were not visible in the accessed listing.

entries.title: Culture Lab LIC continues its gallery-based Sunset Jazz series
entries.development: Millie Gibson performs October 23 at 8 PM in Culture Lab LIC’s recurring intimate gallery jazz series.
entries.significance: The series uses a visual-art venue as regular live-music infrastructure outside Manhattan’s club circuit.
entries.uncertainty: Admission and reservation requirements were not confirmed in the accessed listing.

entries.title: STRATUM seeks artists and editors for its advisory network
entries.development: Newly discovered opportunity: STRATUM Journal invites expressions of interest from scholars, artists, curators, editors and cultural practitioners for its advisory and peer-review network.
entries.significance: The call offers participation in publication infrastructure rather than a one-off exhibition, potentially useful for practitioners working across art and research.
entries.uncertainty: Compensation, term length and selection criteria were not visible in the accessed listing.

sections.title: Occult Practice & Machine Intuition
sections.shortfall: Three distinct research or practice entries met the threshold; two slots remain open.

entries.title: The Smart Machine and the ‘Almost Said’ links divination studies to AI intuition
entries.development: An Oxford TORCH event will examine how divination studies might inform machine ‘intuition,’ distinguishing technical AI research from the broader cultural imaginary of AI.
entries.significance: For IMDO’s Machine Intuition system, the historical link between Turing’s oracle concept and non-mechanical insight offers a precise vocabulary for discussing inference without claiming supernatural access.
entries.uncertainty: This is a humanities argument and event description, not a demonstrated machine capability.

entries.title: Study tests perceived sacredness in AI-assisted tarot
entries.development: Newly discovered research reports three experiments examining how agent identity, interaction modality and question type shape perceived sacredness in AI-assisted tarot.
entries.significance: The design separates who speaks, how the interaction occurs and what is asked, variables that can be preregistered in Noetic Perception Device or Second Sight studies.
entries.uncertainty: Perceived sacredness is a participant response; it does not validate divination or mystical causation.

entries.title: Cross-border paper maps liability around LLM divination
entries.development: A discussion paper connects LLM divination, spiritual-platform economies, sycophancy, therapeutic proximity and foreseeable design effects.
entries.significance: It provides a governance lens for distinguishing symbolic entertainment, spiritual practice and systems that may encourage harmful certainty or dependency.
entries.uncertainty: The paper is a narrative review and proposal, not peer-reviewed causal evidence.
